reasoning.text: The ISO render reads instantly as an open-frame FPGA NTT card — eight glass BRAM banks down the back-left edge, the copper DSP-multiplier column, dark/steel symmetric add/sub pairs in an open rail-and-floor frame, the brass twiddle rail, the blue twiddle ROM, and the ten-fin exploded heatsink all nameable; FRONT/SIDE show nothing sunk below or floating off the ground line. Two real weaknesses persist. First, the headline exploded radix-4 butterfly still reads as a near-empty dark plate in SIDE view and its internal stage order (W1→W2→W3→j-rotator→add/sub→register) is legible only by reading roles, and nothing tells the viewer which of the four fused yokes it explodes. Second, the FPGA die is a featureless grey field in TOP, and crossbar_network still carried a buggy duplicate skewed bank map alongside the committed XOR-fold. The deeper residuals are all source-missing (paper's exact conflict-free map, σ_s, twiddle addressing) and belong to the evidence/amend loop, not geometry.
gaps: SOURCE-MISSING (evidence/amend loop, not geometry): the paper's exact arbitrary-radix conflict-free (bank,offset) functions and per-stage crossbar permutation sigma_s (Sec. III headline) remain the committed XOR-fold stand-in; do not fabricate the paper's construction at the scene layer.

SOURCE-MISSING: twiddle-ROM addressing f(stage,block) under the rearranged twiddle-reuse loop is still the committed CT/bit-reversed layout; the residual bit-reversed-vs-natural-order tension is noted in twiddle_rom spec and cannot be settled visually.
SOURCE-MISSING: exact FSM transition table and per-state cycle latencies beyond the aggregate 9 cycles/lane; schedule_controller holds a reconstructed table only.
SOURCE-MISSING: the naive-radix-4 add/sub baseline (assumed 10) that pins the 20% claim; re-pin if evidence recovers the paper's figure.
SOURCE-MISSING: whether output is genuinely bit-reversal-free in hardware vs computed bit-reversed then relabeled; no geometric encoding can settle this.
SOURCE-MISSING: the specific 14-bit modulus of the paper benchmark (q=12289 is a reproduction fix).
SOURCE-MISSING: host PCIe/DMA framing/handshake on pcb_substrate/host_phy is reproduction-invented.
VISUAL (low residual): the exploded radix-4 unit is inherently near-empty in the −X SIDE projection; the added arrows/callout mitigate but cannot fully populate that single edge-on view.

params.bank_index: b(i) = (i&7) ^ ((i>>3)&7) ^ ((i>>6)&7) ^ ((i>>9)&7)   (committed GF(2)-linear XOR-fold; distinct banks for every power-of-two stride incl. 512)
params.per_stage_permutation: at radix-2 stage s (s=0..9) a butterfly pairs operands at indices (i, i+2^s); because the bank function is GF(2)-linear, b(i) XOR b(i+2^s) = fold(2^s) != 0, so the two operands always land in distinct banks; the crossbar applies the induced read permutation sigma_s mapping lane l <- bank(base_s + l*stride_s) and the write-back applies sigma_s^{-1} so reduced results return to their home banks
params.radix4_routing: a radix-4 BU gathers 4 operands (i, i+2^s, i+2^{s+1}, i+3*2^s) which the XOR-fold guarantees fall in 4 distinct banks; the crossbar routes them to the 4 input ports of one fused lane-pair in a single cycle
params.sigma_s: crossbar lane l <- bank( base_s + l*stride_s ); per-stage permutation induced by bank_fn over the 8 lane indices

before.notes:
Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. Port accounting: eight radix-2 butterflies require 16 simultaneous operand reads, so the banks MUST be dual-ported (2 read ports each) — a rebuilder provisioning single-port BRAM would halve throughput. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map plus the rotation permutation sigma_s satisfy the asserted no-conflict property and are rebuildable by a CS student.
[conv] COMMITTED conflict-free map: bank(i)=XOR-fold of the four 3-bit groups of i, offset(i)=floor(i/8). This is a GF(2)-linear bank function, so for any power-of-two stride 2^k the two operands differ in exactly one address bit and bank(i) XOR bank(i+2^k) = fold(2^k) != 0 -> operands always in distinct banks. [calc] FIXES the verifier counterexample of the prior map b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8: there b(i+512)=b(i) (576 mod 8 = 0) so stride-512 operands collided; with XOR-fold fold(bit9)->bank bit0 = 1 != 0. (bank,offset) is a bijection on [0,1024) (offset fixes bits 9..3, low 3 bits XOR-map to all 8 banks). All human-facing annotations (crossbar/addr_gen/bram) now cite this single committed map; the prior additive form b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8 has been removed as a buggy duplicate. [source-missing] the paper's exact sigma_s crossbar permutation table per stage is not transcribed; the XOR-fold realizes the named property (per-stage 8-way distinctness) but may differ in routing from the paper's specific construction.
Committed a bijective skewed map bank(i)=(i+floor(i/8)) mod 8, offset(i)=floor(i/8): for fixed offset the 8 indices cover all 8 banks, so it is conflict-free for radix-2 and for radix-4 up to stride 16 — this fixes impl-2 FAIL (stride 2^0 r4 collision at i=29) [conv]. The paper's actual arbitrary-radix conflict-free bank-index/offset functions and per-stage crossbar permutation sigma_s (Sec. III headline) are [source-missing] [paper] (FlateDecode PDF body undecodable; eprint/RG mirrors 403). This skewed map is a reproducibility stand-in, NOT the paper's construction; the natural-order/no-bit-reversal datapath the paper claims is also not yet reproduced.
[source-missing] the paper's explicit per-stage crossbar permutation table sigma_s is not transcribed; recorded as the permutation induced by addr_gen_unit's stand-in map.

params.primitive_root_psi: psi = g^6 = 11^6 mod 12289 = 1945 (order 2048; psi^1024 ≡ -1 mod 12289, i.e. negacyclic)
params.j_fourth_root: j = psi^512 (order 4, j^2 ≡ -1 ≡ 12288 mod q); used as the constant rotator by the radix-4 butterflies
params.psi_inv: psi^{-1} mod q via Fermat (psi^{q-2}); INTT uses psi^{-i}/omega^{-k} twiddles together with N^-1 = 12277
params.psi_power_table_sample: entry[k] = psi^k mod 12289 with psi=1945: psi^0=1, psi^1=1945, psi^2=10302(=omega), psi^3=6320, psi^4=3400, ...; structural anchors psi^512=j (j^2≡12288≡-1), psi^1024≡12288≡-1 (negacyclic sign flip), psi^2048≡1; the omega table is the even subsequence omega^k = psi^(2k). The full 0..2047 table is generated by iterated multiply-by-1945-mod-12289 from this seed (bit-exact, no bit-reversal indexing).
params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^i pre-twist and psi^{-i} post-twist factors for the negacyclic case stored in the low/high halves

params.table_contents: entry[s][block] = omega raised to the block's stage exponent (no bit-reversal indexing); negacyclic twist factors keyed by coefficient index i

before.notes:

The radix-4 equations and 3-twiddle assignment recorded here are the basis of the quantified op savings.
[src] the conflict-free mapping is what removes the bit-reversal cost: with the XOR-fold (bank,offset) write addressing applied across all stages, data is consumed/produced in natural order, so no separate permutation pass is needed. Cycle accounting [calc]: r4_stages=5=log4(1024); r4_butterflies_per_stage=256=1024/4; r4_cycles_per_stage=32=256/8 BUs (the bad '64' came from dividing by 4 lanes — the correct divisor is the 8 parallel butterfly units); r4_total_bf_cycles=160=5*32. params.lane_map_radix4: two adjacent radix-2 lanes fuse into one 4-input/3-twiddle radix-4 butterfly -> 8 lanes = 4 radix-4 BUs per cycle
params.radix2_butterfly: Cooley-Tukey: with w=omega^k, u=x0, v=w*x1 -> y0=(u+v) mod q, y1=(u-v) mod q
params.twiddles_per_radix4_BU: 3 twiddle factors W1=w, W2=w^2, W3=w^3, realized as 2 modular multiplications by the symmetric schedule (naive radix-4 uses 3); j=psi^512 is a stored constant rotator, not a fetched twiddle
params.op_counts: optimized radix-4 BU = 2 modular mults + 8 modular add/sub, vs naive radix-4 = 3 modular mults + 10 modular add/sub; the paper's rearranged schedule realizes 33% fewer modular multiplications (1-2/3) and 20% fewer modular add/sub (1-8/10) against the naive radix-4 baseline

after.notes:
Radix-4 fuses two consecutive NTT stages into one pass, the source of the 33% fewer multiplications and 20% fewer add/sub vs the naive radix-4 butterfly; selector also sets address strides in addr_gen and twiddle indexing. The radix-4 equations and 3-twiddle assignment recorded here are the basis of the quantified op savings.
[src] the conflict-free mapping is what removes the bit-reversal cost: with the XOR-fold (bank,offset) write addressing applied across all stages, data is consumed/produced in natural order, so no separate permutation pass is needed. [calc] strides are the DIT stage strides for the selected radix. [conv] radix encoded as the literal value (2 or 4) for the BU array.
radix selectable 2 and 4 [paper: 'scalable radix-2 and radix-4 NTT'] — corrects impl guess '4 only as a butterfly unit'. Optimized radix-4 BU = 2 mults + 8 add/sub vs naive 3 mults + 10 add/sub -> exactly 33%/20% reductions [paper], which fixes the 3-vs-2 mult contradiction: 3 is the NAIVE baseline, 2 is the optimized (realized) count. Cycle accounting [calc]: r4_stages=5=log4(1024); r4_butterflies_per_stage=256=1024/4; r4_cycles_per_stage=32=256/8 BUs (the bad '64' came from dividing by 4 lanes — the correct divisor is the 8 parallel butterfly units); r4_total_bf_cycles=160=5*32. fsm: NEXT_STAGE -> SCALE : stage == last && mode == INTT
NEXT_STAGE -> STORE : stage == last && mode == NTT
transitions: IDLE -> LOAD  [host start pulse]
LOAD -> STAGE_LOOP  [coefficient vector resident in banks]
STAGE_LOOP -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [enter next twiddle-sharing block]
TWIDDLE_FETCH -> BUTTERFLY  [w latched onto broadcast rail]
BUTTERFLY -> REDUCE  [lane products valid]
REDUCE -> WRITEBACK  [r in [0,q) from Barrett stage]
WRITEBACK -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [blocks remain in stage s]
WRITEBACK -> STAGE_LOOP  [stage done, s++ while s<S]
STAGE_LOOP -> INTT_STAGE_LOOP  [forward stages done AND INTT requested]
STAGE_LOOP -> DRAIN  [forward-only transform done]
INTT_STAGE_LOOP -> SCALE_N_INV  [inverse stages done]
SCALE_N_INV -> DRAIN  [coefficients scaled by N^-1]
DRAIN -> IDLE  [output FIFO emptied to host]

[src] read-modify-write interleaved-BRAM loop with 9-cycle pipeline fill per lane. SCALE state runs only for INTT (multiply by Ninv=12277). [conv] state names; rearranged-loop ordering delegated to addr_gen_unit + crossbar_network.
Committed ONE consistent, fully-wired FSM [conv] — resolves the two contradictory state lists and the unwired DONE (DONE now returns to IDLE). INTT path passes through SCALE (multiply by n_inv=12277) before STORE; NTT path skips it. The paper's exact FSM transition table is [source-missing] [paper] (not extractable); this is a minimal correct reconstruction, not transcribed.
[conv] FSM both reverse-impls converged on: IDLE->LOAD->RUN_STAGES->(SCALE_INTT for INTT)->DRAIN->DONE->IDLE; DONE is wired back to IDLE to remove the dangling-state ambiguity prior lists carried. [source-missing] exact transition table and per-state cycle latencies not in retrievable source.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member abutting it, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one fused radix-4 butterfly unit onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the ten-fin exploded aluminum heatsink high onto its riser stub well above the die so the datapath below stays visible.
